Also, have you noticed any swelling or deformities in other joints, such as your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very young age for such symptoms; besides the knee, have you noticed any lumps or bony enlargements on his wrists, knees, or ankles? Also, is there a family history of early-onset joint replacements or bone deformities in his relatives?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right_Knee and Hands

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Systemic or Oligoarticular) with potential misdiagnosis of TB due to family history confusion. 

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, ANA, RF, and HLA-B27. REQUEST IMAGES: Review of the X-Ray reports for erosions or periarticular osteopenia.
